tagline: Shaping the digital future through integrated telecommunications and cloud solutions.
hero_kpi_rationale: Service revenue is the core pillar of Deutsche Telekom's business, representing nearly 83% of total revenue in 2025. It is the most stable and strategic segment, driven by mobile and fixed-line growth, particularly through T-Mobile US.

kpis.name: Service Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from telecom services (mobile, internet, fixed).
kpis.description: Service revenue grows by 2.9% in 2025, driven by T-Mobile US and fiber expansion in Germany.

kpis.name: EBITDA after lease (adjusted)
kpis.explanation: Adjusted operating profit after lease, excluding non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA AL increases for the third consecutive year, supported by synergies and cost management.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow after lease
kpis.explanation: Cash flow available after investments, excluding dividends and spectrum.
kpis.description: FCF AL increases slightly, reflecting capex discipline and strong cash generation.
kpis.signal: Ability to generate cash despite heavy investments.

kpis.name: Net Revenue
kpis.description: Net revenue reaches €119.1B, driven by international operations (78% of total).
kpis.signal: Stable growth despite a competitive environment.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditure excluding spectrum
kpis.explanation: Spending on infrastructure (networks, fiber), excluding frequency licenses.
kpis.description: Capex declines slightly, with a focus on spending efficiency.

kpis.name: Headcount (FTE)
kpis.description: Average headcount decreases slightly, despite growth in the United States.
kpis.signal: Slight contraction, consistent with digitalization and automation.

kpis.name: CO2 Emissions Scope 1+2
kpis.description: Emissions decline by 4.9%, due to energy efficiency and renewable energy adoption.
kpis.signal: Ongoing emission reductions, aligned with climate targets.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.986 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $6.438B in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Proportion of net income distributed as dividends: 67.0% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Mobile Customers
kpis.explanation: Total number of mobile customers worldwide.
kpis.description: Mobile customer base increases by 4.5%, driven by T-Mobile US and customer acquisition strategy.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in the United States with T-Mobile.

kpis.name: Energy Consumption
kpis.explanation: Electricity used by networks and data centers.
kpis.description: Energy consumption is nearly stable, despite growing data traffic.

risks.title: Workforce transformation and large-scale social restructuring
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in provisions (EUR 1.56B restructuring provisions as of 12/31/2025, up EUR 0.2B), with an active 2025 Workforce Transformation program aimed at centralizing teams and eliminating redundancies. Trend stable/increasing over multiple fiscal years.

risks.title: Broadband deployment obligations linked to public subsidies
risks.score_rationale: Liabilities related to publicly funded projects increased by EUR 0.2B to EUR 1.56B, reflecting fiber/broadband deployment obligations conditional on subsidies yet to be received. Regulatory and execution risk in case of failure to meet contractual milestones.

risks.title: Integration and operational risks from the UScellular acquisition
risks.score_rationale: The UScellular acquisition is cited multiple times as a source of increased provisions (site restoration +EUR 0.2B, customer contracts +EUR 0.2B). A recent transaction generating significant integration risks in the US segment, already the largest revenue contributor to the group.

risks.title: Exposure to litigation and rising legal provisions
risks.score_rationale: Provisions for litigation risks amount to EUR 623M at end-2025 (vs EUR 527M at end-2024), an increase of EUR 96M, related to potential settlements of ongoing legal proceedings. Upward trend during the year, without details on underlying cases.

risks.title: Structural dependency on civil servant pension obligations
risks.score_rationale: Deutsche Telekom pays EUR 212M annually to the Civil Service Pension Fund and carries EUR 0.4B in future obligations. A legacy of the Deutsche Bundespost privatization, this liability is non-transferable and subject to German legislative decisions.

risks.title: Dilution risk and capital pressure via T-Mobile US
risks.score_rationale: Transactions with minority shareholders of T-Mobile US reduced equity by EUR 7.5B in 2025 (T-Mobile US share buybacks + DT share disposals). Deutsche Telekom's stake in T-Mobile US is a strategic asset whose valuation and governance are exposed to U.S. market dynamics.

risks.title: Currency risk from consolidation of the U.S. segment
risks.score_rationale: USD/EUR exchange rate effects are cited multiple times as a factor reducing provisions and liabilities (–EUR 0.1B to –0.3B across items). With T-Mobile US representing the majority of consolidated revenue, dollar depreciation structurally impacts euro-denominated reported results.

risks.title: Telecom tower disposals and portfolio asset restructuring
risks.score_rationale: The sale of GD tower companies (tower operations in Germany and Austria), completed on February 1, 2023, is still referenced in 2025 notes, indicating residual adjustments. Such passive infrastructure sales alter cost structure and reliance on third-party operators for site access.

ai_positioning.summary: Deutsche Telekom is gradually integrating AI into its customer and network services, without making it a major strategic pillar. The focus is on automation and operational efficiency.
